Bribe for a Pillow

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An alleged conman is accused of swindling property owners of millions of Rands

Unique Selling Point:
A purported businessman with links to an Eskom contract is allegedly conning property owners to secure free accomodation for Eskom contractors.
That's not all, he's also allegedly bribing Eskom contractors to choose his accommodations over other suppliers.

Summary:
Eugene Swanepoel stands accused of defrauding property owners in the west coast of over R 1 million and stealing luxury sheets.

His con: using his contract to supply Eskom with accommodation as a guarantee of future payment but that’s not all, Swanepoel allegedly bribes Eskom contractors to choose his accommodation over other Eskom suppliers.


Further information:
How does he do it:
Swanepoel approaches property owners who lease their properties out for tourism purposes.
He explains that he has an Eskom contract through his business Bunamanzi.
The contract is legitimate,
The contract is for the supply of accommodation at a local Eskom project.
He then shows the property owners the invoices and legitimate correspondence between him and Eskom.
On this basis, the property owners agree to accommodate Eskom contractors without advance payment in lieu of settlement of the invoices.
Problem is, Swanepoel never settles the amounts owed.
We have three case studies with evidence to back up their complaints against Swanepoel: invoices, POPs, lawyer letters

Running a triple con:
Not only has Swanepoel allegedly conned these property owners, he’s also bribing Eskom contract workers to choose his accommodations over other suppliers.
This is against Eskom rules that contractors must not receive any cash in lieu of any of the services to be provided by suppliers like Swanepoel.
How it’s done: Eskom contractors are supposed to receive three meals a day. Instead of providing the meals, Swanepoel has illegally converted the meals into cash.
Bribing Eskom contractors up to R 19 000 to rather stay with him.

And Swanepoel is using the BEE status of a former lodge worker to secure business from Eskom. He claims to be a business partner but his name doesn’t appear anywhere on the business documents.

Why should anybody care?
Legitimate businesses are being swindled of thousands of Rands using Eskom’s name.
Eskom is already billions of Rands in the red and loopholes like these demonstrate why.
Swanepoel invoices Eskom anywhere up to R 3.6 million - where is this money going because clearly he’s not settling what he owes with the property owners?
Employees within Eskom have been made aware of Swanepoel's activities and yet he continues to access millions of Rands which he doesn’t pay over.

Complainant 1: Chad Simoes

Left R 60 000 in the red with missing luxury sheets.

Chad Simoes owns a number of properties in the area.
He uses them as accommodation for tourists - leisure and business.
During off peak seasons, his properties may remain empty while he still needs to pay the bonds so occupancy is welcome.
So, when he was introduced to Eugene Swanepoel, it seemed the heavens had opened up and rained down financially on his business.

Complainant 2: Margot Odendaal of Margot Cape Stay

Left R 200 000 in the red

Margot Cape Stay manages properties on behalf of clients.
Swanepoel approached Margot with the same story - Bunamanzi is an accommodation placement agent for Eskom and needs properties to accommodate Eskom contractors.
As per usual, Swanepoel did not pay the arrears owed.
Now, Margot has lost clients because of the unsettled debts.

Complainant 3: Cornel Wilsch

Cornel Wilsch is a businessman in theTableview area.
He says he had the misfortune of meeting Swanepoel earlier this year and like Chad, he believed the business gods were shining down on him.
He says Swanepoel employed him at Bunamazi promising a R 100 000 salary a month.

Bribe for A Pillow

(Chad Simoes) I sell houses. I do the long term rentals as well and I mean, even with the Airbnb business, it presents itself some other opportunities.

(Erin) Chad Simoes is a property consultant in Melkbosstrand, west of Cape Town. It’s a place popular with tourists, where short term rentals boom in the summer months.

(Erin) It’s an unpredictable model: make hay while the sun shines and hope for a longer-term deal when the tourists leave.

(Chad Simoes) So from April all the way up until the end of September, then we try and secure a tenant. It's not always possible, but that's the ideal scenario.

(Erin) Luckily Melkbostrand is home to Eskom’s nuclear power plant, Koeberg, which hosts a near-constant flow of out-of-town contractors who need somewhere to stay.

(Erin) But, where Eskom is involved, controversy is never far away. This is a story about another alleged conman enriching himself at the parastatal’s expense.

(Erin) It’s a surprisingly successful, if unsophisticated scam and at its centre is the simple need… for a bed.

(Erin) A short walk from Melkbostrand’s main beach is a boutique guest lodge co-managed by Cornel Wilsch.

(Cornel Wilsch) Primarily it’s businessmen, corporates at ranges between one thousand to two thousand Rand a day.

(Erin) Sometimes, demand outstrips what the lodge can manage.

(Cornel Wilsch) As it turns out, ever so often, there is not enough space to accommodate everybody in these premises, and we will outsource it to fellow guest houses and people we’re affiliated with.

(Erin) It’s an environment ripe for an enterprising middleman to step in.

(Erin) And it’s precisely such a middleman that the property managers say they fell victim to earlier this year. His name is Eugene Viljoen.

(Erin) Through a company called Bunamanzi Holdings, he finds and books accommodation for Eskom workers and contractors.

(Cornel Wilsch) He can arrive here in his slops and shorts, and you'll think he's just somebody that's come to visit, and he's here for a braai.

(Erin) Chad’s first impressions of Eugene weren’t any better.

(Chad Simoes) Yeah, sketchy. I'm not going to lie. He didn't come across very presentable. Very rough around the edges.

(Chad Simoes) But I like to think I did my due diligence at least having to find out he had the contract.

(Erin) Viljoen had thirty Eskom contractors to house in Melkbosstrand. He claimed to have worked with Eskom for more than two decades, handing over documents supposedly proving he was legit.

(Erin) But, six months later, Cornel, Chad and others, are out of pocket to the tune of more than a million Rand.

(Erin) How did he behave when you asked for your money?
(Chad Simoes) He constantly came up with excuses. He seemed very hyper. He's a very, very hyper guy.

(Erin) Viljoen’s excuse for not paying? ANOTHER middleman - trading as Travel With Flair - owed HIM money…

(Chad Simoes) This is the message that he sent through, the performance is just stunning. So, have a listen here.

(Voice Recording)(TWF Employee) I know you’re not good.
(Eugene) And this is not right
(Eugene) I've got people breathing down my neck and I’m a very angry client—

(Erin) Viljoen peppered them with voicenotes like this one, supposedly proving that Travel With Flair, or TWF had failed to pay him.

(Erin) If you’re confused, we don’t blame you. Simply put, Eskom uses TWF to manage all contractors’ travel arrangements. But TWF opted to outsource its responsibilities to middlemen: Viljoen being one of them. Viljoen is ultimately responsible for paying the accommodation bill. But, in Chad and Cornel’s cases, that payment never happened.

(Erin) Chad says Viljoen owes him R62 000. Cornel’s unpaid debts come to 750 000.

(Erin) No story about government contracts would be complete without: you guessed it - allegations of bribery.

(Cornel Wilsch) The first time that I saw a white envelope passed on to a contractor - I approached Eugene he said, it's a lucky packet. I said, what the hell is a lucky packet?

(Cornel Wilsch) He says, no, it's the money we give them so they can look after themselves, buy their own food.

(Erin) It sounds innocent enough but direct payments to contractors shouldn’t even be possible. Since Eskom covers contractors’ meals, no cash should ever change hands and this is made clear on the document issued by TWF.

(Erin) So, why does Viljoen insist on giving contractors cash for food that’s already been paid for?

(Cornel Wilsch) I went and found vouchers for them: for R200 for breakfast, R200 for supper and R200 for lunch.

(Cornel Wilsch) Eugene at that point said no, no, we're going to pay them cash.The money that he offered them was what blew my mind.

(Cornel Wilsch) Eugene said they needed to get R900 a day.

(Erin) R900 a day for food?

(Cornel Wilsch) For food.

(Erin) R900 - in cash - every day: it’s a powerful incentive for contractors to choose Viljoen as their travel agent.

(Cornel Wilsch) So he said, ‘Cornel, this is the way it gets done.

(Cornel Wilsch) So we just pay them more and then we'll get them.’This is how the industry works and Eskom knows it.’

(Erin) If you believe Viljoen, Eskom’s suppliers are in a bidding war, with these so-called food allowances now a cash grab for contractors.

(Cornel Wilsch) So when they land, they demand their first week's payment.

(Erin) In fact, Viljoen’s lucky packets have become such common practice that Eskom contractors complain when payment isn’t received.

(Eugene) Eugene, he gave me R 5600 and he knows very well I'm a fortnight person - he just take a chance by doing that to me - this is not right at all!

(Erin) And here’s Viljoen - assuring his “customers” that the money is on its way.

(Eugene) You must remember, I'm the one paying you guys - please you're not going to intimidate me anymore regarding monies or whatever.

(Erin) With “lucky packets” of up to R 19 000, these Eskom contractors were making a killing just by laying their heads on a pillow. In just one month, the bribes amounted to over three hundred thousand Rand.

(Erin) When payments stalled for some, they allegedly complained about non-existent issues with their rooms, before packing their bags and moving in with the competition.

(Cornel Wilsch) When I asked them to tell me why they're leaving and they said, we haven't been paid our money.

(Erin) Again, none of this should be possible. Because if Eskom covers accommodation and meals, there’s no reason for Viljoen to be making payment arrangements with the contractors directly. Somehow, contractors have found a way to exploit the system and they’re pitting service providers - like Viljoen - against each other. Whoever offers the biggest ‘lucky packet’ gets the business.

(Erin) So, how exactly is Viljoen cashing in on this scheme? Cornel wondered the same thing after the numbers didn’t add up. Remember this TWF voucher? It shows that TWF paid Viljoen R1680 for food and accommodation per day. Since the contractor would stay at lodges like Cornel’s and others for 30 days, the standard rates were negotiated down to R700 per night. So, that leaves R980. Subtract Viljoen’s generous R900 lucky packet, and he’s left with a measly R80 in profit.

(Erin) Even at the reduced rate of R700 per day, if you add another R900 cash, you're into R1,600. That's almost all the money. Where's the profit?

(Cornel Wilsch) There is no profit left at that point

(Erin) It seems the only way for Viljoen to make a profit is to keep the R700 meant for the room, leaving hotel and lodge owners out of pocket.

(Erin) Wanting answers, we pack our bags and travel to Vanderbijl Park in Gauteng to confront Viljoen.

(Erin) Hi I'm Erin from Carte Blanche, it’s lovely to meet you.

(Eugene) Oh good and you, good good

(Erin) Eugene we have some very serious questions to ask you about your accommodation down in Melkbos…

(Erin) Viljoen acknowledges his debt, but claims it’s nowhere near a million rand.

(Eugene Viljoen) No I said, we will pay them off my lawyer is busy currently with their lawyers to strike a deal

(Erin) So it's a payment plan?

(Eugene Viljoen) Absolutely

(Erin) OK

(Erin) And what's the hold up
(Eugene Viljoen) We're just waiting for money to come in.
(Erin) From?

(Eugene Viljoen) Business that we do.

(Erin) We also wanted to find out more about the alleged lucky packets…

(Erin) What is a lucky packet?

(Eugene Viljoen) Tell me what is a lucky packet, I don't know anything about lucky packets.

(Erin) The lucky packets that you are giving to contractors at Eskom.

(Eugene Viljoen) That's not true.

(Erin) We have audio of you speaking to Eskom contractors about money to be paid directly into their accounts.

(Eugene Viljoen) No, that's not true.

(Erin) I can play one for you.

(Eugene Viljoen) Please do

(Eugene Viljoen) [You must remember, I'm the one paying you guys]

(Erin) That's your voice.

(Eugene Viljoen) OK is that a problem?

(Eugene Viljoen) If I pay for electricity into their account, or if I out of good faith and will sponsor them for a night. Is that a crime?

(Erin) Well from what I understand and I've seen the vouchers from TWF - Travel With Flair— and it says very clearly there in the terms and conditions, that the vouchers, let me finish please, the vouchers may not be exchanged for monies.

(Eugene Viljoen) Umm you know when you start working with these people and you stay for long you become a family.

(Erin) The allegation is that your are giving them a premium amount of R 900 a day - a day - for their food

(Eugene Viljoen) Excuse me?!

(Erin) Viljoen does the sums for us - and as expected, they don’t add up.

(Eugene Viljoen) Did they tell you this, if you say the rate is 1680, how can you give someone R 900 and still pay the accommodation. How's that possible, it doesn't make sense.

(Erin) If he does pay the R900, Viljoen says, it’s a necessary expense.

(Erin) On what.. Let's drill down, electricity and?

(Eugene Viljoen) Partying a lot of other things

(Erin) Like?

(Eugene Viljoen) I don't give money for food I don’t do that - I honour my deal with TWF and I honour my deal with Eskom.

(Erin) So, electricity, water and partying?

(Eugene Viljoen) What is the problem with it? What is the problem?

(Erin) It's bribery!

(Eugene Viljoen) I'm not bribing anyone.

(Erin) Not in Melkbosstrand, that is.

(Eugene Viljoen) We have withdrawn ourselves there.

(Erin) Why?

(Eugene Viljoen) Just didn't work out for us.

(Erin) Why not? Were you paying too many bribes?

(Erin) TWF refused to comment. Eskom says it has no contractual relationship with Bunamanzi Holdings or Eugene Viljoen. It says Eugene Viljoen is TWF’s employee. Following our queries, Eskom says it’s referred the matter to the Hawks.

(Erin) Meanwhile, the con continues to play out - on you, the taxpayer, covering the cost of the luxury accommodation and lucrative lucky packets.

(Erin) So, why does Viljoen insist on giving contractors cash for food that’s already been paid for? (Cornel Wilsch) I went and found vouchers for them: for R200 for breakfast, R200 for supper and R200 for lunch. (Cornel Wilsch) Eugene at that point said no, no, we're going to pay them cash.The money that he offered them was what blew my mind. (Cornel Wilsch) Eugene said they needed to get R900 a day. (Erin) R900 a day for food? (Cornel Wilsch) For food. (Erin) R900 - in cash - every day: it’s a powerful incentive for contractors to choose Viljoen as their travel agent. (Cornel Wilsch) So he said, ‘Cornel, this is the way it gets done. (Cornel Wilsch) So we just pay them more and then we'll get them.’This is how the industry works and Eskom knows it.’ (Erin) If you believe Viljoen, Eskom’s suppliers are in a bidding war, with these so-called food allowances now a cash grab for contractors. (Cornel Wilsch) So when they land, they demand their first week's payment. (Erin) In fact, Viljoen’s lucky packets have become such common practice that Eskom contractors complain when payment isn’t received. (Eugene) Eugene, he gave me R 5600 and he knows very well I'm a fortnight person - he just take a chance by doing that to me - this is not right at all! (Erin) And here’s Viljoen - assuring his “customers” that the money is on its way. (Eugene) You must remember, I'm the one paying you guys - please you're not going to intimidate me anymore regarding monies or whatever. (Erin) With “lucky packets” of up to R 19 000, these Eskom contractors were making a killing just by laying their heads on a pillow. In just one month, the bribes amounted to over three hundred thousand Rand. (Erin) When payments stalled for some, they allegedly complained about non-existent issues with their rooms, before packing their bags and moving in with the competition. (Cornel Wilsch) When I asked them to tell me why they're leaving and they said, we haven't been paid our money. (Erin) Again, none of this should be possible. Because if Eskom covers accommodation and meals, there’s no reason for Viljoen to be making payment arrangements with the contractors directly. Somehow, contractors have found a way to exploit the system and they’re pitting service providers - like Viljoen - against each other. Whoever offers the biggest ‘lucky packet’ gets the business. (Erin) So, how exactly is Viljoen cashing in on this scheme? Cornel wondered the same thing after the numbers didn’t add up. Remember this TWF voucher? It shows that TWF paid Viljoen R1680 for food and accommodation per day. Since the contractor would stay at lodges like Cornel’s and others for 30 days, the standard rates were negotiated down to R700 per night. So, that leaves R980. Subtract Viljoen’s generous R900 lucky packet, and he’s left with a measly R80 in profit. (Erin) Even at the reduced rate of R700 per day, if you add another R900 cash, you're into R1,600. That's almost all the money. Where's the profit? (Cornel Wilsch) There is no profit left at that point (Erin) It seems the only way for Viljoen to make a profit is to keep the R700 meant for the room, leaving hotel and lodge owners out of pocket. (Erin) Wanting answers, we pack our bags and travel to Vanderbijl Park in Gauteng to confront Viljoen. (Erin) Hi I'm Erin from Carte Blanche, it’s lovely to meet you. (Eugene) Oh good and you, good good (Erin) Eugene we have some very serious questions to ask you about your accommodation down in Melkbos… (Erin) Viljoen acknowledges his debt, but claims it’s nowhere near a million rand. (Eugene Viljoen) No I said, we will pay them off my lawyer is busy currently with their lawyers to strike a deal (Erin) So it's a payment plan? (Eugene Viljoen) Absolutely (Erin) OK (Erin) And what's the hold up (Eugene Viljoen) We're just waiting for money to come in. (Erin) From? (Eugene Viljoen) Business that we do. (Erin) We also wanted to find out more about the alleged lucky packets… (Erin) What is a lucky packet? (Eugene Viljoen) Tell me what is a lucky packet, I don't know anything about lucky packets. (Erin) The lucky packets that you are giving to contractors at Eskom. (Eugene Viljoen) That's not true. (Erin) We have audio of you speaking to Eskom contractors about money to be paid directly into their accounts. (Eugene Viljoen) No, that's not true. (Erin) I can play one for you. (Eugene Viljoen) Please do (Eugene Viljoen) [You must remember, I'm the one paying you guys] (Erin) That's your voice. (Eugene Viljoen) OK is that a problem? (Eugene Viljoen) If I pay for electricity into their account, or if I out of good faith and will sponsor them for a night. Is that a crime? (Erin) Well from what I understand and I've seen the vouchers from TWF - Travel With Flair— and it says very clearly there in the terms and conditions, that the vouchers, let me finish please, the vouchers may not be exchanged for monies. (Eugene Viljoen) Umm you know when you start working with these people and you stay for long you become a family. (Erin) The allegation is that your are giving them a premium amount of R 900 a day - a day - for their food (Eugene Viljoen) Excuse me?! (Erin) Viljoen does the sums for us - and as expected, they don’t add up. (Eugene Viljoen) Did they tell you this, if you say the rate is 1680, how can you give someone R 900 and still pay the accommodation. How's that possible, it doesn't make sense. (Erin) If he does pay the R900, Viljoen says, it’s a necessary expense. (Erin) On what.. Let's drill down, electricity and? (Eugene Viljoen) Partying a lot of other things (Erin) Like? (Eugene Viljoen) I don't give money for food I don’t do that - I honour my deal with TWF and I honour my deal with Eskom. (Erin) So, electricity, water and partying? (Eugene Viljoen) What is the problem with it? What is the problem? (Erin) It's bribery! (Eugene Viljoen) I'm not bribing anyone. (Erin) Not in Melkbosstrand, that is. (Eugene Viljoen) We have withdrawn ourselves there. (Erin) Why? (Eugene Viljoen) Just didn't work out for us. (Erin) Why not? Were you paying too many bribes? (Erin) TWF refused to comment. Eskom says it has no contractual relationship with Bunamanzi Holdings or Eugene Viljoen. It says Eugene Viljoen is TWF’s employee. Following our queries, Eskom says it’s referred the matter to the Hawks. (Erin) Meanwhile, the con continues to play out - on you, the taxpayer, covering the cost of the luxury accommodation and lucrative lucky packets.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): An alleged conman is accused of swindling property owners of millions of Rands
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A purported businessman with links to an Eskom contract is allegedly conning property owners to secure free accomodation for Eskom contractors. That's not all, he's also allegedly bribing Eskom contractors to choose his accommodations over other suppliers.
metadata.Summary: Eugene Swanepoel stands accused of defrauding property owners in the west coast of over R 1 million and stealing luxury sheets. His con: using his contract to supply Eskom with accommodation as a guarantee of future payment but that’s not all, Swanepoel allegedly bribes Eskom contractors to choose his accommodation over other Eskom suppliers.
metadata.Further information: How does he do it: Swanepoel approaches property owners who lease their properties out for tourism purposes. He explains that he has an Eskom contract through his business Bunamanzi. The contract is legitimate, The contract is for the supply of accommodation at a local Eskom project. He then shows the property owners the invoices and legitimate correspondence between him and Eskom. On this basis, the property owners agree to accommodate Eskom contractors without advance payment in lieu of settlement of the invoices. Problem is, Swanepoel never settles the amounts owed. We have three case studies with evidence to back up their complaints against Swanepoel: invoices, POPs, lawyer letters Running a triple con: Not only has Swanepoel allegedly conned these property owners, he’s also bribing Eskom contract workers to choose his accommodations over other suppliers. This is against Eskom rules that contractors must not receive any cash in lieu of any of the services to be provided by suppliers like Swanepoel. How it’s done: Eskom contractors are supposed to receive three meals a day. Instead of providing the meals, Swanepoel has illegally converted the meals into cash. Bribing Eskom contractors up to R 19 000 to rather stay with him. And Swanepoel is using the BEE status of a former lodge worker to secure business from Eskom. He claims to be a business partner but his name doesn’t appear anywhere on the business documents. Why should anybody care? Legitimate businesses are being swindled of thousands of Rands using Eskom’s name. Eskom is already billions of Rands in the red and loopholes like these demonstrate why. Swanepoel invoices Eskom anywhere up to R 3.6 million - where is this money going because clearly he’s not settling what he owes with the property owners? Employees within Eskom have been made aware of Swanepoel's activities and yet he continues to access millions of Rands which he doesn’t pay over. Complainant 1: Chad Simoes Left R 60 000 in the red with missing luxury sheets. Chad Simoes owns a number of properties in the area. He uses them as accommodation for tourists - leisure and business. During off peak seasons, his properties may remain empty while he still needs to pay the bonds so occupancy is welcome. So, when he was introduced to Eugene Swanepoel, it seemed the heavens had opened up and rained down financially on his business. Complainant 2: Margot Odendaal of Margot Cape Stay Left R 200 000 in the red Margot Cape Stay manages properties on behalf of clients. Swanepoel approached Margot with the same story - Bunamanzi is an accommodation placement agent for Eskom and needs properties to accommodate Eskom contractors. As per usual, Swanepoel did not pay the arrears owed. Now, Margot has lost clients because of the unsettled debts. Complainant 3: Cornel Wilsch Cornel Wilsch is a businessman in theTableview area. He says he had the misfortune of meeting Swanepoel earlier this year and like Chad, he believed the business gods were shining down on him. He says Swanepoel employed him at Bunamazi promising a R 100 000 salary a month.
